Off the southern coast of Taiwan, where turquoise water hides teeth of coral, a shipwreck in 1867 left more than broken timber behind. Decades later, a handful of bones surfaced near Da Wan Beach, and with them, something that refused to stay buried.

This is the story of the Eight Treasures Princess. 🕯️

Part of an ongoing series narrating Taiwan's ghost stories, countryside legends, and local deity folklore in English. 🎥 Full story on YouTube — link in bio and pinned in the comments.

This is a retelling based on Taiwanese folklore and urban legend, written for atmosphere — not a historical documentary.

This is the moment the story turns.

On a quiet Taichung university campus, a stone bridge crosses a shallow creek — twelve steps, always twelve, students have counted them a thousand times.

But cross alone at midnight, and some nights your foot finds a thirteenth step that shouldn't exist. 🌙

A soft voice may ask you the time. It may ask about a young man who never came. Whatever you do, don't answer, and don't look back.

This is the moment her silence finally broke.

In old Qing-era Tainan, a widow named Chen Shou-niang made a quiet promise to honor her late husband's memory forever — a vow that should have been hers alone to keep.

When a covetous clerk and her own family conspired against her for refusing to break it, the walled city's narrow lanes bore witness to a cruelty the neighbors could hear but not stop. 🕯️

What followed reached far beyond her death, into the halls of the county government itself, where footsteps still seem to linger long after the lanterns burn low.
